Date... Sept. 21, 36.

Subject Local National Salvation Association entertains
Chinese journalists on September 19.
Made by D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by Whitman, S.S.

Leading members of the local national salvation
associations entertained some 25 local Chinese journalists
to dinner in the Dinty Moore Restaurant, 35 Ningpo Road,
at 7 p.m. September 19, 1936. Sung Chun-dz (沈鈞儒),
leader of the Cultural Circles National Salvation
Association, who presided, gave a brief report of the
incident on September 18 when members of the Chinese
Police assaulted pedestrians without first explaining
that the service in connection with the erection of a
tablet to commemorate the September 18 Anniversary, had
been prohibited. The attendance was subsequently
informed that the following demands had been submitted
to the Chinese Authorities :-
1. That the officials responsible for the incident be
punished.
2. That Martial Law be abolished and protection be
afforded to the patriotic movement.
3. That a guarantee be given against a repetition of
this procedure.
4. That compensation be granted to the persons injured
during the incident.
In conclusion, the reporters were urged to render
assistance by maintaining justice and publishing authentic
news regarding the national salvation movement.
The function terminated at 9.30 p.m.

Sih Tse Liang
D. I.
Officer i/c Special Branch.

日期……1936年9月21日。

主题：本地救国会于9月19日宴请中国记者。
由督察 Sih Tse-liang 制作，由 Whitman, S.S. 转呈。

1936年9月19日下午7时，本地救国会的主要成员在宁波路35号 Dinty Moore 餐厅设宴款待了约25名本地中国记者。文化界救国会领袖沈鈞儒（Sung Chun-dz）担任主席，他简要通报了9月18日发生的事件，当时中国警察在未事先解释为纪念九一八事变而立碑的活动已被禁止的情况下，袭击了行人。随后向与会者通报，已向中国当局提出以下要求：
1. 惩处对该事件负责的官员。
2. 废除戒严令，并为爱国运动提供保护。
3. 保证不再重演此类行为。
4. 对在事件中受伤的人员给予赔偿。
最后，敦促记者们通过维护正义和发布关于救国运动的真实新闻来提供协助。
活动于晚上9时30分结束。

Sih Tse Liang
督察
特务科主管。

A - 过去五年日本侵华的历史

1) 日本侵华的目的是为了解决其国内政治和财政困难，消除英美在远东的影响，并为入侵苏联铺平道路。九一八事变是其正式开启侵华战争的标志。

2) 自九一八事变以来，中国失去了辽宁、黑龙江、吉林和热河东北四省。冀东地区建立了所谓的防共自治政权，从而与中国分离，而河北、察哈尔、绥远和蒙古则设立了半独立的政治委员会。中国也被剥夺了在上海驻军的权利。

3) 九一八事变后，中国不仅丧失了对日本占领领土的主权，也丧失了对该国其他地区的主权，因为日本走私者可以公开进行活动，而中国人民的爱国运动则在日本的指使下受到本国政府的镇压。

B - 中国在过去五年中遭受的损失及吸取的教训

1) 中国从九一八事变中吸取的第一个教训是，日本是其死敌。

2) 第二个教训是，中国可以与苏联和法国结盟以对抗日本。

3) 第三个教训是，中国可以通过抵抗外来侵略来避免灭亡。

C - 当前的严峻形势及民众的职责

为迎接即将到来的九一八事变周年纪念日，我们必须支持并参加抵制走私运动和国货推广运动。我们必须支持

上海各界民众救国联合会成立一八五周年紀念宣言

同胞們！在今年以前，日本帝國主義對我國的侵略，已經歷了五十年的漫長時期。在這五十年中，中國人民遭受了無數的苦難和犧牲。從甲午戰爭到九一八事變，從七七事變到抗戰勝利，我們始終沒有屈服於敵人的淫威之下。今天，當我們紀念這個具有歷史意義的日子時，我們應該更加堅定地團結起來，為實現祖國的完全統一和民族的偉大復興而努力奮鬥！

回顧過去，我們可以看到，正是由於全國人民的共同努力，才使得我們能夠戰勝強大的敵人，取得最後的勝利。然而，我們也不能忘記那些為了國家獨立和民族解放而英勇獻身的先烈們。他們的精神將永遠激勵着我們前進！

展望未來，我們面臨著新的挑戰和機遇。在全球化的背景下，我們需要進一步加強與世界各國的合作交流，共同應對各種全球性問題。同時，我們也要繼續堅持改革開放的基本國策，推動經濟社會持續健康發展。

讓我們攜手並肩，以更加昂揚的姿態迎接未來的挑戰，為建設一個富強民主文明和諧美麗的社會主義現代化強國而不懈奮鬥！

（印：上海各界民眾救國聯合會）
（批：此宣言於一九三五年十二月九日發表）

1936年9月19日下午4时40分，特别处副督察 Lees 打来电话称，接获南市公共安全局情报，当地全国救国会成员拟于1936年9月19日晚7时，在宁波路35号 Dinty Moore 咖啡馆宴请若干记者，届时将介绍1936年9月18日举行的示威游行情况。当地爱国协会的高级成员也拟在同一时间和地点举行会议。

警方约谈了 Dinty Moore 咖啡馆的管理层，并警告其不得允许在店内举行任何具有政治性质的集会。

据管理层透露，一位李先生和一位秦先生已安排于1936年9月19日晚7时宴请约二三十位朋友用餐。

1936年9月19日晚7时，李公樸（量才夜校校长，校址南京路大陆商场345室）和沈钧儒（上海法學院院长，校址江湾路）抵达。李先生，

who is known to be a highly placed member of the National

Mr. Tsin and himself had invited a number of journalistic
and other friends to dinner, a procedure which they
follow once a month.

They were interviewed by Ch. Insp.Bishop, Officer-
in-charge Central Station, D.S. Pitts, Special Branch,
and the undersigned, and warned against holding a meeting
of a political nature. Mr. Lee gave an undertaking that
no such meeting was contemplated. He also suggested that
a number of detectives should attend the meeting to watch
the proceedings.

In all twenty-nine persons attended the dinner,
this party mostly composed of local journalists. The
party dispersed at 9.40 p.m. 19-9-36.

During the course of the dinner Lee Kong Pao,Tsin
Kying Tsze and three other members addressed the party,
and protested against the action of officers of the
Bureau of Public Safety, Nantao, in the manner in which
they dealt with the members of the procession formed in
Nantao, on the 18-9-36, in commemoration of the 5th
Anniversary of the September the 18th Incident. It was
proposed that the Mayor of Greater Shanghai be informed
and called upon to deal in a severe manner with the
offending officers of the force.

Subject Pictures, maps, cartoons to commemorate the 5th anniversary of the
Mukden Affair (18/9/31.) found distributed to 2 shops on Y'poo Road.
Made by D.S.I. Liu Wen Chao Forwarded by [Signature] Inspt. Officer i/c.

Sir:-
At 8:30 p.m. on 17/9/36, C.D.C. 108 brought to the station
2 maps, 2 handbills with cartoons and pictures to commemorate the
5th anniversary of the Mukden Affair September 18, 1931, pub-
lished by the Shanghai Various Circles Salvation Federation,
which the detective received from a shopkeeper named Zien Tuh
Nyi (錢德義), at No. 2461 Yangtsepoo Road at about 8:15 p.m.
even date, whilst passing the above shop on patrol on Yangtsepoo
Road.
The above named shopkeeper when interviewed by C.D.C. 108
and the undersigned, stated that at about 8 p.m. on 17/9/36,
when he and his assistants were busily engaged with their custom-
ers, a Chinese boy of about 16-17 years of age threw over the
counter of the shop 4 handbills with maps, cartoons and pictures
printed. The boy was closely followed by a male of student type
who approached the shop people and called their attentions to
the commemoration of the 5th anniversary of the Mukden Affair
which falls on 18/9/36, (tomorrow). As the people in the shop
were too busy to give attention to his words, they walked away
in eastern direction along Yangtsepoo Road. Another cartoon
was found to have been distributed to the Woo Tung (沪东) stock-
ings shop, No. 2481 Yangtsepoo Road. Patrol made by detectives
along Yangtsepoo Road failed to locate the 2 men as described
above, who were responsible for the distribution of the handbills
which are respectfully submitted for information. Teleprinter
message re same has been circulated to all stations and all
precautionary measures are being taken by detectives as well as
uniform men on patrol against possible disturbance by radicals.
I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
D. S. I.

由副督察刘文超呈报 转呈者 [签名] 负责督察。

敬启者：
1936年9月17日晚8时30分，C.D.C. 108 号侦探将两张地图、两份印有漫画和图片以纪念1931年9月18日“九一八”事变五周年的传单带至巡捕房，这些物品是他在同日晚上约8时15分巡逻经过杨树浦路时，从杨树浦路2461号一家店主钱德义（音译）处收到的。

Sir,
At 7 p.m. 17-9-36 a telephone message was received at the station by S.I. Oikawa from 226 Kinchow Road to the effect that girl students were distributing anti Japanese pamphlets.
D.S. White, J.D.C. 149, C.D.C. 37 and the undersigned attended, but on arrival found all quiet.
From one Mr. A. Nakahara who owns a medicine shop at No. 226 Kinchow Road, it was ascertained that at about 6.50 p.m., 4 Chinese girls of the student type had proceeded along Kinchow Road and Ward Road giving pamphlets to the shop keepers and others.
Mr. Nakahara handed to the undersigned three pamphlets which had been thrown into his shop.
Translation as follows:-
1. The fifth anniversary of Sept. 18th.
2. To memorise Sept. 18th and assist the North East volunteer corps.
3. To clean up the words Sept. 18th with blood and sweat.
4. Drive out the Japanese robbers.
5. Down with the creator of invasion, the Japanese Imperialism.
Published by the United Salvation Society of Shanghai.
Police patrolled the district, but the girls could not be found and nothing untoward occurred.
S.I.
Noted
Phyl.
I am, Sir,

To the Commissioner of Police,

I beg to inform you that the following instructions

"Since the outbreak of the Chengtu and Pakhoi
incidents, a tense situation has been created in Shanghai.

create disturbances in Shanghai on or about September 18,
and in order to adopt the necessary precautionary measures,

declared martial law in the district of Shanghai effective
from September 17 till September 20. During this period,
no meetings, processions, suspension of studies, strikes,

be dealt with in accordance with law. The precautionary
measures will be undertaken by the Bureau of Public Safety
with the assistance of the Pao An Tuan and Military Police.
Special attention must be paid to the following points:-

1. Increase the number of policemen on duty in the vicinity
of shops or residences of foreigners or at strategic
points.

2. Organize patrolling parties during this period and
patrol places frequently visited by foreigners.

The 5th"Anniversary of the September 18 Incident " : Possible happenings.

Information indicates that members of the Shanghai Various Circles National Salvation Federation, remnants of the Chinese People's Armed Self-Defence Association, and certain pro-communist elements, under the auspices of the Third Party, have planned to assemble at 3 p.m. to-day, September 18, near Marche de l'Est - border between Chinese controlled territory and French Concession - and then proceed via Avenue Edward VII, the Bund, Broadway, Wayside, Yangtsepoo Road, Liping Road, to Pingliang Road Market and Kungping Road Market, for the purpose of holding"flying" meetings. It is reported that the majority of participants will consist of students of either sex.

The same informant adds that mill workers in the Eastern District will gather outside their respective concerns to await and join the oncoming demonstrators. Supervisors and messengers are reported to have been provided in the various districts to direct the procession.

According to information from reliable sources, genuine "inner" members of the local communist fraternity have been ordered not to participate in any possible happenings and those who do participate in any demonstration will be communist sympathisers only.

near Dalny Road did publicly incite others to transgress the

Summary Court North A.M.

Mr. Wong appeared for the S.M.C.

Proceedings:- Mr. Wong:- The Accused is charged under Art.153 of the
C.C.C. When arrested, this Accused was found in possession of
eight handbills bearing inscriptions and pictures detrimental to
the Japanese. Nowadays when the Chinese Government clearly
expresses to renew friendly relationship with Japan, the Accused's
action is to be considered as publicly inciting others to trans-
gress the law. The Accused did not deny distributing the hand-
bills but stated that they had been given to him by one Lao Liu.
However, he could not give evidence to prove same. The
Accused, although cannot read, was once a member of the Communist
Party. It is unknown whether the Accused distributed the
anti-Japanese handbills for some other purpose.

handbills ?

to distribute same. I did not know the contents of the hand-
bills. According to Lao Liu, they only contained some pictures.

WOO KYUNG PEH ( 吴金发 )
Tsingkiangpu                                D.S. Jones
Wayside Stn.        Sept.17,1936            Clerk King Hsin-kuo

    My name is Woo Kyung Peh , age 25, native of Tsingkiang,
Kiangsu.  My father, who operated a clothier's shop at
Tsingkiang, died when I was seven.  Two years later I was
brought to Shanghai by my relatives who came here in search
of employment.  My mother got a job in the Pootung Tobacco
Factory of the B.A.T.
    I have never been to school and cannot read or write.
                                          a
    At the age of 15 I obtained job in the B.A.T. Factory
Pootung.  I was there for one year and then became a peddler
of toys for 2 years.  Then for 1½ years I worked in the Leaf
Department of the No.2 B.A.T. Factory at Pootung.  At the age
of 20 I left this factory at the instigation of one Shiang
Teng Yung ( 向长荣 ), who advised me to join the
Communist Party in Kiangsi Province.  I left Shanghai in
company with one Woo Ah Yung ( 吴巧荣 ), to Siuching Hsien.
There I was employed making twenty cent silver coins for use
in the Communist districts.  For this work I was paid $15
a month.  I did no other communist work.  After two years
at this place I escaped because conditions were so hard.
I made my way to Kanchow, thence to Shensi ( 陕西 ),
Kiangsi, where I joined the Central Government army.  After
six months I obtained leave and came to Shanghai.  This was
in March, 1935.  I was unemployed until August and then
began work as a cigarette hawker, my present occupation.
    For the past four months I have resided at No.188
Ming Yuen Fang ( 明园坊 ), Ward Road.

吴金发 ( WOO KYUNG PEH )
清江浦                                警佐 Jones
路边巡捕房        1936年9月17日            书记员 金新国 (King Hsin-kuo)

    我叫吴金发，25岁，江苏清江人。我父亲在清江经营一家裁缝店，在我七岁时去世。两年后，亲戚来上海谋生，将我带至上海。母亲在英美烟草公司浦东烟厂找到一份工作。
    我从未上过学，不识字，也不会写字。
                                          a
    15岁时，我在英美烟草公司浦东工厂找到一份工作。我在那里工作了一年，随后做了两年的玩具小贩。之后，我在英美烟草公司浦东第二厂的烟叶部工作了1年半。20岁时，在向长荣（Shiang Teng Yung）的唆使下，我离开了这家工厂，他劝我加入江西省的共产党。我与吴巧荣（Woo Ah Yung）一同离开上海，前往修水县。在那里，我受雇为共产党地区制造面值二角的银币。此项工作月薪15元。我没有从事其他共产党工作。在那里待了两年后，因条件艰苦，我逃了出来。我辗转来到赣州，继而前往陕西、江西，在那里加入了中央政府军队。六个月后，我获准休假并来到上海。那是1935年3月。我一直失业到8月，随后开始做香烟小贩，即我目前的职业。
    过去四个月，我居住在华德路明园坊188号。

Date 17th Sept., 1936.

REPORT

Subject Arrest of a male Chinese in possession of anti-Japanese handbills.

Made by D.S. Hall. Forwarded by

Sir,
At 7.50 p.m. 17-9-36, C.P.C.2230 brought to the station one
Woo Kyung Feh (吴京发), 25, Tsirgkising, s/hawker, 108, Ming
Yuen Faung, Ward Road, whom he had arrested at 7.40 p.m. ever date
on Wayside Road near Walny Road. At the time of his arrest,
accused was engaged in distributing hardbills of an anti-Japanese
nature. Eight of these hardbills were found in his possession.
Questioned by C.D.C.248 and the undersigned, accused stated
that a newsvendor named Lau Liu (老刘), whereabouts unknown,
had given him the pamphlets on Dongshen Road near Kwenming Road
and asked him to distribute them. Accused states that Lau Liu
told him that the handbills were maps. Accused, who is illiter-
ate, maintains that he was unaware of the nature of the
literature which he was engaged in distributing.
The hardbills in question bear the heading "In memory of
September 18th 1931. Shanghai National Salvation Union. Resist
the invaders of China. Down with Japanese Imperialism". There
are four illustrations symbolical of Japan's occupation of China.
The Special Branch was informed and D.S. Jones attended.
The accused was interrogated by him and the attached statement
taken. One copy of the pamphlet was retained for the use of the
Special Branch.
Accused will appear before Court on 18-9-36 when application
will be made for a writ of Detention in respect of the accused.
I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
(签名)
Senior Det. 1/c. D.S. Hall

报告

主题：逮捕一名持有反日传单的华籍男子。

由警佐 Hall 制作。转呈

先生，
1936年9月17日下午7时50分，华捕2230号将一名叫吴京发（Woo Kyung Feh）的男子带到巡捕房，该男子25岁，籍贯清江兴（Tsirgkising），职业小贩，住址华德路明园坊108号。他于同日晚上7时40分在路边路靠近华伦路处被捕。被捕时，被告正在分发具有反日性质的传单。在他身上发现了八张此类传单。经华探248号及本人讯问，被告称一名名叫老刘（Lau Liu）的报贩（下落不明）在邓森路靠近昆明路处将小册子交给他，并请他分发。被告称，老刘告诉他这些传单是地图。被告是文盲，坚称他不知道他所分发的文献的性质。
涉案传单标题为“纪念一九三一年九月十八日。上海救国会。抵抗中国侵略者。打倒日本帝国主义”。有四幅象征日本占领中国的插图。
已通知特别部门，警佐 Jones 到场。他对被告进行了审讯，并记录了附带的供词。保留了一份小册子副本供特别部门使用。
被告将于1936年9月18日出庭，届时将申请对被告发出拘留令。
此致，
敬礼，
(签名)
高级侦探主管 警佐 Hall

Woo Kyung Fah 吴金荣，
Tsingkiangpu D.S. Jones
Wayside Stn. Sept.17,1936 Clerk King Hsin-kee

My name is Woo Kyung Fah , age 25, native of Tsingkiang,
Kiangsu. My father, who operated a clothier's shop at
Tsingkiang, died when I was seven. Two years later I was
brought to Shanghai by my relatives who came here in search
of employment. My mother got a job in the Peotung Tobacco
Factory of the B.A.T.

I have never been to school and cannot read or write.
At the age of 15 I obtained a job in the B.A.T. Factory
Peotung. I was there for one year and then became a peddler
of toys for 2 years. Then for 1½ years I worked in the Leaf
Department of the No.2 B.A.T. Factory at Peotung. At the age
of 20 I left this factory at the instigation of one Shiang
Tang Yung (向长荣), who advised me to join the
Communist Party in Kiangsi Province. I left Shanghai in
company with one Woo Ah Yung (吴阿荣), to Sining Hsien.
There I was employed making twenty cent silver coins for use
in the Communist districts. For this work I was paid $15
a month. I did no other communist work. After two years
at this place I escaped because conditions were so hard.
I may my way to Kanchow, thence to Shanchman (陕川),
Kiangsi, where I joined the Central Government army. After
six months I obtained leave and came to Shanghai. This was
in March, 1935. I was unemployed until August and then
began work as a cigarette hawker, my present occupation.

For the past four months I have resided at No.106
Ming Yuen Fang (明园坊), Ward Road.

我叫吴金发，25岁，江苏清江人。我父亲在清江经营一家裁缝店，在我七岁时去世。两年后，亲戚来上海谋生，将我带至上海。母亲在英美烟草公司浦东烟厂找到一份工作。

我从未上过学，不识字，也不会写字。
15岁时，我在英美烟草公司浦东工厂找到一份工作。我在那里工作了一年，随后做了两年的玩具小贩。之后，我在英美烟草公司浦东第二厂的烟叶部工作了1年半。20岁时，在向长荣（Shiang Tang Yung）的唆使下，我离开了这家工厂，他劝我加入江西省的共产党。我与吴阿荣（Woo Ah Yung）一同离开上海，前往西宁（Sining）县。在那里，我受雇为共产党地区制造面值二角的银币。此项工作月薪15元。我没有从事其他共产党工作。在那里待了两年后，因条件艰苦，我逃了出来。我辗转来到赣州，继而前往陕川（Shanchman）、江西，在那里加入了中央政府军队。六个月后，我获准休假并来到上海。那是1935年3月。我一直失业到8月，随后开始做香烟小贩，即我目前的职业。

过去四个月，我居住在华德路明园坊106号。

Writ of Detention.

At 12 midnight 17-9-36, P.S. 209 A.W. Smith was on duty near the corner of Weihaiwei and Chungking Roads when he noticed the 2 accuseds walking towards him on Chungking Road. The 1st accused was carrying a bundle wrapped in newspaper under his arm and a blue enamel mug of paste in his hand. The 2nd accused was found to have in his pockets a bundle of posters. On the way to the Station the 1st accused attempted to escape, and in the struggle his jacket was torn at the neck.

Enquiries made at the station by the undersigned and C.D.S. 219 ascertained that the papers found in the possession of accuseds were of an Anti-Japanese nature.

Statements were taken from accused wherein they state that their names are:- 1st accused Ching Kwoh Zee (金國全), 18 years, native of Ningpo, 3/employed, at a small factory, Zau Ka Do, Village where he has been employed for the last 11 days since arriving in Shanghai from Ningpo where he previously studied at the Ching Hai Primary School for six years.

My name is Ching Kwoh Zee, 18 years, native of Ningpo,
& employed, for the past 11 days as a copper smith in a
small factory in Jou in Do Village.
I arrived in Shanghai 11 days ago from Ningpo where I
studied in the Chin Wei Primary School for 6 years.
At 8p.m. 17-9-36, I with my friend named Tsang Ko Tsung
(arrested) were walking on Racecourse near Mohawk Roads when
we met one named Kyung Ts Kwong (金之光), whom I knew in
Ningpo. This person gave me a parcel of paper and an enamel
mug of paste and told me to paste them on the walls on various
roads, but I did not paste any posters on the wall. I do

我叫金國全，18岁，宁波人，
过去11天在邹家渡村的一家小工厂担任铜匠。
我于11天前从宁波来到上海，此前我在振威小学读了6年书。
1936年9月17日晚上8点，我和我的朋友曾科宗（已逮捕）在莫霍克路附近的跑马场行走时，
遇到了一位名叫金之光 (Kyung Ts Kwong) 的人，我在宁波认识他。此人给了我一包纸和一搪瓷杯浆糊，
让我把它们贴在各种道路的墙壁上，但我并没有在墙上张贴任何海报。
我不理解我被外国巡捕在重庆路逮捕时所携带的海报的含义。

Dah-lee                                  xx C.D.S.219.

My name is Tsang Ko Sun 17 years, native of Dah Lee,
s/unemployed, residing in Hau Ho Do Village. In May 1931,
I arrived in Shanghai from Dah Lee and obtained employment
in Her Tsang Iron Works on Kwouming Road which lasted until
20th of August 1931, when the factory closed down owing to the
depression, and from that time on I have been unemployed,
    A fellow worker named Ching Kwoh Zee (arrested) native
of Ningpo and who worked with me in the Iron Works on Xwenming
Road, and now resides with me in Zau Ka Do Village. Neither
of us had anything to do today 17-9-36 so we walked to
Shanghai and at about 9p.m. or 10p.m. on Chungking Road we
met a friend of Ching Kwoh Zee's, who's name I do not know.
This person handed over to Ching Kwoh Zee some printed papers
which he told us to post on the various walls on the roadway.
We had only posted 2 papers on the wall in Chungking Road when
we were both arrested by a Policeman and I had in my possession
picture posters.
    I do not understand the meaning of the posters nor do I
know where they were printed or why we should post them on
the walls. All the above is my true statements.
(signed)
                                        Signed:- Tsang Ko Sun.

我叫張國成，17岁，大里人，
无业，居住在好浩渡村。1931年5月，
我从大里来到上海，在国明路的赫昌铁厂找到工作，一直做到
1931年8月20日，当时工厂因萧条而关闭，从那时起我一直失业。
一位名叫金國全（已逮捕）的同事，宁波人，曾和我一起在
国明路的铁厂工作，现在和我住在赵家渡村。
1936年9月17日今天我们要都没事做，所以我们走到
上海，大约在晚上9点或10点在重庆路我们
遇到了金國全的一位朋友，我不知道他的名字。
此人交给金國全一些印刷品，
让我们贴在道路旁的各种墙壁上。
我们只在重庆路的墙上贴了2张纸，
就被一名巡捕逮捕了，我当时持有图片海报。
    我不理解这些海报的含义，也不知道它们是在哪里印刷的，
或者为什么我们要把它们贴在墙上。以上均为我的真实陈述。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 16, 1936

SHANGHAI TROUBLE
IS FEARED

Japanese Intelligence
On Next Friday's
Anniversary

MUKDEN INCIDENT DATE
'AND STUDENTS' PLANS

Japanese diplomatic and navy officials in Shanghai gathered aboard the cruiser Idzumo, flagship of the Japanese Third Fleet, yesterday afternoon for a two-hour discussion of the increasingly involved situation in South China and to study intelligence reports forecasting the possibility of rioting in Shanghai on September 18, the fifth anniversary of the Mukden Incident. The Idzumo is moored to the N.Y.K. Mail Wharf adjoining the Japanese Consulate-General.

While the exchange of views on the Pakhoi issue is understood to have been limited to a review of information on hand, the officials are reported to have examined in detail forecasts of probable disturbances on Friday.

According to this advance information, the Shanghai General National Salvation Association and the China Students' National

Salvation Federation are planning to stage a mass meeting and a parade on Friday. Handbills announcing these plans are understood to be ready for distribution beginning to-day.

A campaign for the collection of funds to erect a memorial of the incident is also reported to have been projected.

Riots Alleged Planned

Other reports told of alleged plans of the Racial and National Salvation Federation, a South-Western group, to assassinate Japanese officials in Shanghai and to instigate riots in the three municipal areas.

Attending the conference were: Vice-Admiral Koshiro Oikawa, commander of the Third Fleet; Rear-Admiral Seiichi Iwamura, chief of staff of the fleet; Consul-General Kaname Wakasugi; Mr. Toyoichi Nakamura, Consul-General in Canton, who stopped here yesterday on his way south; Tateki Horiuchi, Consul-General in Tientsin who is visiting here; Mr. Akiyoshi Tajiri, first secretary of the Embassy; Lieut.-Commander Matao Okino, assistant naval attache and Mr. Noritake Yoshioka, third secretary in charge of press relations.

Martial Law Here

In view of numerous reports that demonstrations and disturbances would mark the anniversary of the Mukden Incident, martial law has been proclaimed in the Shanghai area with effect from Thursday until Sunday. General Yang Hu, Commander-in-Chief of the Shanghai-Woosung Garrison, has forbidden meetings, distribution of handbills and disturbances of any kind.

日本驻上海的外交和海军官员昨日下午聚集在日本第三舰队旗舰“出云”号巡洋舰上，进行了两小时的讨论，议题为华南日益复杂的局势，并研究预测9月18日（即“九一八”事变五周年纪念日）上海可能发生骚乱的情报报告。“出云”号停泊在毗邻日本总领事馆的日本邮船会社（N.Y.K.）邮件码头。

据悉，关于北海问题的意见交流仅限于对现有信息的回顾，但据报道，官员们详细审查了关于周五可能发生的动荡的预测。

据报道，还策划了一场募集资金以建立事变纪念碑的运动。

此地戒严

鉴于有多份报告称示威和骚乱将标志“九一八”事变纪念日，上海地区已宣布实行戒严，自周四起生效至周日。沪淞卫戍区总司令杨虎将军禁止任何形式的集会、分发传单和骚乱。

Extract from Intelligence Report of September 16, 1936.

Anniversary of Mukden Incident - September 18

There is no indication that communists will observe this anniversary. The Shanghai Various Circles National Salvation Federation, however, plan to hold a mass meeting of an anti-Japanese character in the Chinese Chamber of Commerce on that day, but the Chinese Authorities state they will take effective steps to prevent it. The People's Educational Institute Ling Chung Choral Corps, another anti-Japanese organization, proposes to hold a choral programme at 9 a.m. September 18 in the Lecturing Hall of the Wen Miao Park (Chinese controlled territory). This programme will likewise be prohibited by the Chinese Authorities.

Apart from these two items there is nothing to indicate that anti-Japanese or radical elements plan any street demonstrations, although baulked in respect of having the Chamber of Commerce as a meeting place they may make quick plans to convene gatherings elsewhere.

Taking into consideration the facts that radical propaganda in respect of this day has not been extensive and that September 18 falls on a week day, the chances of a demonstration or disorder of any magnitude being staged in the Settlement are very remote.

The Woosung-Shanghai Defence Commissioner has declared martial law in Chinese controlled territory from September 17 to 20 inclusive, while the City Government has issued a proclamation prohibiting the delivering of speeches liable to impair the good relations with friendly Powers.

All Stations.

"The Council claims that our discharge would
effect a saving in expenditure. As a matter of fact, the
amount of the wages of 1,000 road coolies is less than the

is acting harshly towards the lower class Chinese
employees.
"Roads have been extended and widened; moreover,
repairs to roads are increasing because of the damage done
by heavy traffic. The Council should employ more coolies.
Then, why is the Council discharging us?
"Of late, the workers of various trades have
demanded an increase of wages, but we, road coolies, have
carried on our work as usual. During the Sino-Japanese
Hostilities in Shanghai in January, 1932, all the defence
works were constructed by us under showers of bullets and
many of us were killed or wounded. How can the Council be
so hard-hearted? The Council has shown no consideration
for our meritorious work.
"The Council is acting unreasonably. Its decision
to discharge road coolies shows that it despises the Chinese.
We pledge to fight for our case and shall not give up until
it has been settled to our satisfaction."

National Herald and other local newspapers :-
PRESIDENT OF PHILIPPINE ISLANDS DUE HERE JANUARY 28
At 4.45 p.m. yesterday, Mr. C.E. Gauss,
American Consul-General in Shanghai, received an official
telegram from Mr. Manuel Quezon, President of the Philippine
Commonwealth Government, stating that he is leaving Hongkong
by the s.s. "Empress of Canada" and will arrive in Shanghai
at noon January 28. As soon as he received the wire, Mr.
Gauss formally notified the prominent members of the local
American community as well as Mayor Wu Teh Chen, General
Yang Hu, and others so that a welcome may be accorded the
President on his arrival.
It is learned that the s.s. "Empress of
Canada" will arrive in Shanghai at 1 p.m. to-morrow and
will berth at the Shanghai & Hongkew Wharf. Prominent
Chinese and foreign members of the local community will be
at the wharf to welcome President Quezon.
It is also learned that Mr. Gauss will give
a tea party in honour of Mr. Quezon at 4 p.m. to-morrow at
his official residence on Amherst Avenue. Many prominent
persons will be invited.
Between 6 and 8 p.m. to-morrow, Mayor Wu
Teh Chen will entertain Mr. Quezon to dinner at the Park
Hotel.
Dr. H.H. Kung, Minister of Finance, will
come to Shanghai and will entertain Mr. Quezon to dinner
at 9 p.m. to-morrow; the venue has not yet been fixed.
Mr. Quezon will remain in Shanghai for one
night and will leave by the same steamer at 9.30 a.m.
January 29 for America where he will call on Mr. Roosevelt,
President of the United States of America.

CINEMATOGRAPHS TO BE ORDERED TO EXHIBIT PARTY AND NATIONAL

audience must be made to stand up as a mark of respect.
It is learned that this order has not yet been
sent to Shanghai.

Lih Pao (brief comment)):-

A DATE WE SHALL NEVER FORGET.

To-day is the 5th anniversary of the seizure of the Three Eastern Provinces by another country. These provinces have an area of 4,650,000 square li with a population of 40,000,000. These people are being treated like slaves.

Anniversary of Mukden Incident, September 18
- Demonstration in Nantao

In connection with the observance of the fifth
anniversary of the Mukden Incident, September 18, a
demonstration was staged in Nantao by the members of
various national salvation societies. The participants
commenced to assemble at 2 p.m. on Tung Meng Road, between
the Small East Gate and the Nantao Bund. At 3.30 p.m.
the number had increased to 500, and upon the arrival of
Wong Chao-dz ( 王造時 ) and Sze Liang, leaders of the
Cultural and Women's Circles National Salvation Associations
respectively, a procession was formed and proceeded west
along Min Kuo Road. Apart from singing songs and shouting
slogans of an anti-Japanese nature, the processionists
chalked slogans on walls, tramcars, ricshas and other
vehicles. At West Gate the procession was held up by a
large party of Police and Peace Preservation Corps. The
participants however ignored all requests to disperse
quietly and were eventually broken up by force. In the
melee three policemen and several processionists were
injured. Two of the participants were later arrested.

Beyond the arrest of two persons for distributing
anti-Japanese literature no untoward incident occurred in
the Settlement. These two individuals together with three
of the four apprehended on September 17 are held on a writ of
detention, four until September 21, and one until September 23.
The fourth man arrested on September 17 was released owing
to lack of evidence.

九一八事变周年，9月18日
- 南市示威

为纪念九一八事变五周年，9月18日，各救国会成员在南市举行示威。参与者于下午2时开始在小东门与南外滩之间的同盟路集结。下午3时30分，人数增至500人，随着文化界和妇女界救国会领导人王造时（Wong Chao-dz）和施良（Sze Liang，音译）的到来，队伍组成并沿民国路向西行进。除了演唱歌曲和高呼反日口号外，示威者还在墙壁、电车、人力车和其他车辆上用粉笔书写标语。在西城门，游行队伍被大批警察和保安队拦阻。然而，参与者无视所有和平解散的要求，最终被武力驱散。在混战中，三名警察和数名示威者受伤。两名参与者随后被捕。

除两人因散发反日宣传品被捕外，租界内未发生其他不幸事件。这两人与9月17日被捕的四名中的三人一起被拘留，其中四人拘留至9月21日，一人拘留至9月23日。9月17日逮捕的第四人因证据不足被释放。

Anniversary of Mukden Incident - September 18

There is no indication that communists will observe
this anniversary. The Shanghai Various Circles National
Salvation Federation, however, plan to hold a mass meeting
of an anti-Japanese character in the Chinese Chamber of
Commerce on that day, but the Chinese Authorities state
they will take effective steps to prevent it. The People's
Educational Institute Ming Chung Choral Corps, another
anti-Japanese organization, proposes to hold a choral
programme at 9 a.m. September 13 in the Lecturing Hall of
the Wen Miao Park (Chinese controlled territory). This
programme will likewise be prohibited by the Chinese
Authorities.

Apart from these two items there is nothing to
indicate that anti-Japanese or radical elements plan any
street demonstrations, although baulked in respect of
having the Chamber of Commerce as a meeting place they
may make quick plans to convene gatherings elsewhere.

Taking into consideration the facts that radical
propaganda in respect of this day has not been extensive
and that September 18 falls on a week day, the chances of
a demonstration or disorder of any magnitude being staged
in the Settlement are very remote.

The Woosung-Shanghai Defence Commissioner has
declared martial law in Chinese controlled territory from
September 17 to 20 inclusive, while the City Government
has issued a proclamation prohibiting the delivering of
speeches liable to impair the good relations with friendly
Powers.

- 2 -

九一八事变纪念日——9月18日

目前并无迹象表明共产党人会纪念这一周年。然而，上海各界救国联合会计划于当日在中国商会举行一场具有反日性质的大会，但中国当局表示将采取有效措施予以阻止。另一反日组织人民教育馆明钟合唱团提议于9月13日上午9时在文庙公园讲堂（华界）举行合唱节目。该节目同样将被中国当局禁止。

除上述两项外，并无迹象表明反日或激进分子计划进行任何街头示威，尽管他们在利用商会作为集会地点方面受阻，但他们可能会迅速策划在其他地方召集聚会。

考虑到针对这一天的激进宣传并不广泛，且9月18日为工作日，在租界内发生大规模示威或骚乱的可能性微乎其微。

吴淞上海防卫委员已宣布在华界自9月17日至20日（含首尾两日）实行戒严，同时市政府发布告示，禁止发表可能损害与友好邦交关系的言论。

OSAKA JOURNALIST
ATTACKED

Objection to Photographer of
Mob Demonstrations Here

Mr. Takeshi Nagato, a member of
the local office of the "Osaka Asahi,"
a leading Japanese daily, was rescued
by a French policeman as he was
about to be assaulted by men of
the Peace Preservation Corps in
Nantao, the "Shanghai Nichi-Nichi"
reported.

The newspaperman was taking
photographs of the soldiers as they
were preparing to block the path of
demonstrators, marking the fifth an-
niversary of the Mukden Incident,
when he was threatened by the
guards, the journal said.

A French policeman, passing by,
saw Mr. Nagato's predicament and
placing the reporter in his car, took
him to the French Police head-
quarters. The newspaperman was
later transferred to the Japanese
Consulate-General.

Meanwhile, the Peace Preservation
Corps, according to the daily, has
asked the French Police, through the
Public Safety Bureau, for the sur-
render of photographs taken by Mr.
Nagato.

进一步检查发现，静安寺路723号一家中国家具店的窗户上用中文刻有“反对日本帝国主义关系”字样。

The manager of this shop was questioned, but he denied dealing in Japanese goods or being connected with them in any way.

The damage in every instance is superficial and does not necessitate the removal of the glass.

It is believed that these offences were committed before 2 a.m. this morning, as there is a restaurant and a cafe in the same block of shops which close at 2 a.m. and both these shop windows were untouched.

It is believed that the person who committed these offences used either a glass cutter or a sharpened piece of steel and walking from West to East scratched every window pane he passed with the exception of those protected by iron gates or with lights in the window.

Between the times these offences were committed, 3 uniform and 1 plain clothes C.P.U. were patrolling Bubbling Well Road between Chinhai Road and Moulmein Road. One patrolman was also passing this particular block of shops once every hour.

Bubbling Well Road and vicinity was patrolled by D.S.I. White and S.I. Goffe, the latter i/c of a Search party between 2 a.m. and 3 a.m. 19-9-36, but none of the aforementioned police officers observed anything unusual or met with any suspicious persons.

It would be impossible to notice any of the scratches at night.
